modes.title: Draw and Repayment Periods
modes.description: Model an interest-only draw period followed by fully amortizing repayment.
modes.formula: Average draw payment = balance × monthly interest + annual fee/12 during draw only; repayment amortizes the balance without the annual fee.
output_labels: Net initial proceeds after closing costs
assumptions: Assumes the full outstanding balance exists at the start, stays constant through draw, and the rate stays fixed. The annual fee is a recurring account-maintenance charge during the draw period only; it stops in the repayment period. Enter 0 if your lender has no annual fee. For average monthly draw payments and this estimated APR, the annual fee is spread across 12 draw-period months; partial draw years are prorated. Actual annual billing dates can change cash-flow APR. Closing costs are a dollar amount or a percentage of the loan. Upfront payment uses outside cash; deduction reduces the disbursed cash. Both reduce net initial proceeds for APR without changing contractual principal. This model does not finance closing costs on top of the loan.

modes.title: Maximum Credit
modes.description: Estimate the maximum additional home equity credit from a lender’s combined loan-to-value ceiling.
modes.formula: Maximum credit = home value × maximum LTV − outstanding mortgage balance.

entries.title: IRR Calculator
entries.implementation_policy: Reference-informed independent calculations; expert fallback explicitly authorized where source behavior is not observable

modes.title: Fixed Cash Flow
modes.description: Estimate an effective annual IRR from equally spaced fixed cash flows; choose frequency and beginning/end timing.
modes.formula: NPV = Σ CFₜ/(1+r)^t = 0.
assumptions: All headline rates are effective annual IRRs. Initial investment is a positive amount entered here and is converted into a negative time-zero outflow. Subsequent negative flows represent additional investment; zeros preserve empty periods.

The numerical search is bounded to approximately −99.9994% through 16,275,379% per year. Multiple or repeated roots can exist; detected roots are not a guarantee that every root was found. Nearly repeated roots are numerically sensitive. IRR is not ROI and does not measure risk.

Cash-flow frequency: Annually. Final value is received at the exact end of the holding period. For a partial final period, only recurring payment dates within the holding period are included; no prorated recurring payment is invented. Additional investment treats the entered periodic amount as an outflow. The no-recurring-flow selection ignores the periodic amount.

modes.title: Unequal Annual Cash Flows
modes.description: Estimate an annual IRR from unequal amounts at successive year ends. Amounts may vary, but dates remain one year apart.
modes.formula: NPV = Σ CFₜ/(1+r)^t = 0.
assumptions: All headline rates are effective annual IRRs. Initial investment is a positive amount entered here and is converted into a negative time-zero outflow. Subsequent negative flows represent additional investment; zeros preserve empty periods.

The numerical search is bounded to approximately −99.9994% through 16,275,379% per year. Multiple or repeated roots can exist; detected roots are not a guarantee that every root was found. Nearly repeated roots are numerically sensitive. IRR is not ROI and does not measure risk.

modes.title: Required Savings
modes.description: Estimate the retirement balance needed to fund an inflation-adjusted income gap.
modes.formula: Target = sum of first-year income gap × (1 + inflation)^(year − 1) / (1 + return)^year; required monthly saving funds target less future current savings.
assumptions: The entered income gap is the first retirement-year withdrawal, paid at that year’s end; inflation increases subsequent yearly withdrawals. A dollar income target is an annual amount at retirement; a percentage applies to projected final working income. Monthly savings are paid at month end; annual savings at year end; salary-percentage deposits are paid monthly and increase with the entered annual income increase. Other income is treated as inflation-indexed throughout retirement. Returns and inflation remain constant.

modes.title: Saving Plan
modes.description: Find the periodic saving needed to reach a retirement target.
modes.formula: Monthly saving = (target − future current savings)/annuity accumulation factor.
assumptions: Monthly savings are paid at each month end. Annual total of monthly savings is twelve monthly deposits; Required year-end annual saving is an alternative single deposit at each year end. These are separate plans, not amounts to contribute together. Annual return is an effective annual rate.

modes.title: Monthly Withdrawal
modes.description: Estimate the initial sustainable monthly withdrawal with subsequent inflation increases.
modes.formula: Retirement balance includes current savings, month-end deposits and additional year-end deposits. Initial monthly withdrawal = retirement balance × (1 + monthly inflation) / real-rate monthly annuity present-value factor.
assumptions: First withdrawal is at the end of the first retirement month. Subsequent monthly withdrawals grow at the monthly rate equivalent to entered annual inflation. Monthly contributions occur at month end; additional annual contributions occur at year end, both before retirement. Annual investment return is effective.

modes.title: Savings Longevity
modes.description: Find how long a retirement balance supports fixed monthly withdrawals.
modes.formula: N = −ln(1 − PV×i/PMT)/ln(1+i); actual month-end withdrawals use ceil(N), with the last withdrawal capped at the available balance.
assumptions: Withdrawals occur at month end after investment returns. Duration ends on the actual final payment date; the final withdrawal is limited to the remaining balance. Annual return is effective and constant; taxes and fees are excluded.

entries.title: 401K Calculator
entries.implementation_policy: Reference-informed independent calculations; expert fallback explicitly authorized where source behavior is not observable

modes.title: 401(k) Projection
modes.description: Project savings one year at a time. Starting balance plus employee contributions includes the starting 401(k) balance plus the sum of each projected year’s capped employee contribution.
modes.formula: For each year: employee = min(annual salary × contribution%, age-based annual limit); employer = min(employee, annual salary × match limit%) × match%; ending balance = opening balance × (1 + annual return) + employee + employer. Starting balance plus employee contributions = starting 401(k) balance + sum of annual employee amounts.
assumptions: Retirement income uses the entered life expectancy. Annual return is effective; monthly withdrawals increase at the monthly-equivalent inflation rate. Constant returns, full vesting and no taxes or fees are assumed. This is a sustainable-withdrawal illustration, not an RMD calculation or a guarantee.

Annual iteration: the entered salary applies to the first projection year; salary increases once after each year. Each year’s employee contribution is salary × contribution percentage, capped by the limit for your age at the start of that projection year. Starting balance plus employee contributions adds the entered starting 401(k) balance once to the sum of these annual employee amounts. It excludes future investment returns and future employer matching; the starting balance may already contain past employer contributions and returns. The Employee column shows only that year’s new employee contribution.

The opening balance earns the entered annual return first, then employee and employer contributions are added at year end. All projected years use 2026 limits with age-based catch-up; future limit increases are not projected. Employer matching uses up to $360,000 of compensation; annual additions excluding catch-up are capped at the lesser of compensation or $72,000. Catch-up deferrals above the regular employee limit are excluded from that additions cap. Other employers’ plans and nondiscrimination tests are not modeled. Calculations retain full precision; displayed annual amounts are rounded.

modes.title: Early Withdrawal Cost
modes.description: Estimate income tax and the additional early-distribution penalty.
modes.formula: Net withdrawal = gross − marginal income tax − applicable 10% additional tax.

inputs.label: Still employed by the employer sponsoring this account?
Left this employer in or after the year you turned 55?
Other early withdrawal penalty exception applies?

assumptions: Intended for distributions before age 59½. The 10% additional tax is waived for a selected qualifying disability, another selected exception, or separation from this employer in or after the year you turn 55 when no longer employed by that sponsoring employer. The age-55 rule does not generally apply to IRAs; plan eligibility must be checked. Income tax still applies. This marginal-rate illustration does not recalculate a complete tax return.

modes.title: Maximize Employer Match
modes.description: Find a steady contribution-rate window for two matching bands without reaching the employee limit early.
modes.formula: Employer match = first band × first match rate + additional band × second match rate.
output_labels: Minimum contribution rate for full match
assumptions: A steady contribution rate from 5.0000% through 30.6250% can earn the full modeled match without exhausting the employee limit early. Use the unrounded result when setting payroll elections.

Assumes equal pay across the year, a constant contribution percentage, per-pay-period matching, no annual true-up, no prior year-to-date contributions and full-year employment. The maximum is a conservative rate that avoids reaching the limit before year end; it does not optimize the final payroll’s partial contribution. Employer matching uses the 2026 $360,000 eligible-compensation cap and the $72,000 annual-additions cap excluding employee catch-up. A large match can be reduced by this additions cap. Actual plan rules, other employers and prior contributions may further restrict contributions.

Second tier is the additional band after tier one, not a cumulative upper threshold. The employee limit uses your entered age and fixed 2026 rules; no employer match is available if both tier match rates are zero.
